full_judgment: 4. Mr. M. Yousuf Ali the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that petitioner No. 1 got allotment of the Plot No. 18 & 19 having 4,000 sqm, area of Sector-1 of Uttara EPZ under PS. and District Nilphamari for the purpose of establishment of export oriented electrical Capacitor industry. Ultimately petitioner No. 1 imported the machineries but due to shortage of working capital the petitioner No. 1, -M/s Kapric Electronics (BD) Ltd. has failed to go on production the capacitor for export in terms of lease deed. Annexure-A to the petition though all those imported machineries have been kept within the BEPZA area where custom authority had / has nothing to interfere in order to impose tax and duty since section 15 of the BEPZA Act, 1980 has so exempted which is to be used in the export processing Zone So, finding no other alternatives petitioner No. 1 . has taken a positive step with the permission of the lessor (BEPZA) to .transfer the land, building and other material and equipments in favour of petitioner No.2; foreign investor, in terms of an agreement Annexure-C to the petition on payment of all dues of BEPZA to run the export oriented industry generating work for 1000 of workers peoples of the locality. He further submits that by this time petitioner has paid the entire dues payable to BEPZA and thereafter BEPZA has withdrawn the very cancellation of the Plot which was done at the instance of respondent Nos. 2 and 3, However, in no way tax can be imposed on the machineries imported by the petitioner, the allottee of the export processing Zone, who has failed to go on production so far. He goes to argue that since there is no specific period of limitation for establishment of the industry, respondent Nos.1, 2, 3, have no authority to impose taxes; as such the very imposition of impugned tax is absolutely illegal and without lawful authority. The learned-Advocate further submits that Section 15 of the Bangladesh Export Processing Zone Act, 1980 read with SRO 544-L/84/888/Cus dated 10-12-1984 has clearly ousted the jurisdiction of the custom authority to impose any tax as soon as any imported goods is entered into the BEPZA Zone.
